purpose: Hardens the WP 7.1+ client-side media processing integration: new uploads receive server-side dominant-color/LQIP placeholder extraction (now reachable even when get_format() returns 'none'), the frontend stops re-queueing missing conversions on every view when client-side processing is active, and heic/heif MIME mappings were added for accurate preload types.
riskRationale: All three iteration-1 issues (filter reachability, decompression-bomb dimension guard, needless GD decode) are correctly fixed and verified, and the new decode is gated by placeholderType plus the same filesize/dimension guards as convert_image(). Risk is medium rather than low because the branch commits the full require-dev Composer tree (~4,700 files, ~525k insertions) into the tracked vendor/ directory against AGENTS.md's production-only convention, and placeholder data is stored only for the full-size original so sub-size renders silently fall back to SVG. No PII, auth, or injection concerns.

text: The functional fixes are correct and well-scoped: placeholder extraction is now reachable in the default WP 7.1 configuration, memory-guarded before any decode, and gated on a consuming placeholderType; the re-queue suppression preserves serving of already-converted images; and the MIME mappings are IANA-correct. Two important issues remain before merge: the branch commits ~4,700 dev-only vendor files against the documented production-only convention, and the client-side placeholder path stores data only for the original file while the frontend looks placeholders up by rendered sub-size URLs. A handful of minor robustness and polish gaps also remain in the new helper.

reasoning: The three previously reported correctness issues are resolved and the core logic is sound, but the branch commits the full dev-dependency tree into tracked vendor/ in violation of the repo convention, and placeholder data is keyed only to the full-size original so the PR's headline outcome does not hold for the sub-size renders that dominate frontend markup. Both are mechanical to fix and an automated agent can resolve them safely.

message: The reachability fix is exactly right: the wp_generate_attachment_metadata filter is now registered when client-side media processing is enabled even when get_format() returns 'none' (the default WP 7.1 mapping), so the placeholder branch in convert_image_to_next_gen_format() actually runs in the primary scenario the previous review flagged.

The new getimagesize() + wppo_max_dimensions (5000x5000) guard is applied before imagecreatefromstring(), mirroring convert_image() exactly: headers-only parsing cheaply rejects decompression bombs before any pixel data is decoded, closing the memory-exhaustion gap on the synchronous upload request path.

Gating the client-side decode on placeholderType being 'dominant_color' or 'lqip' avoids needless full-file reads and GD decodes for the default 'svg'/'none' configs while staying consistent with the consumption side (get_placeholder_type() reads the same option key).

The re-queue suppression in maybe_serve_next_gen_image() is precisely scoped: only the add_img_into_queue() calls are short-circuited when client-side processing is active, while the file_exists() branches that serve already-converted images are untouched, so existing conversions and legacy queue state are preserved.
heic -> image/heic and heif -> image/heif match the IANA-registered MIME types and are safe to emit in preload link type attributes.

The branch commits the entire development Composer tree into the tracked vendor/ directory (~4,700 files, ~525k insertions: phpunit, antecedent/patchwork, brain/monkey, mockery, hamcrest, sebastian/*, nikic/php-parser, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, etc.). AGENTS.md explicitly requires committing production-only vendor after 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader); master's vendor/ has ~236 files vs ~4,967 here. Most of these dev packages are NOT excluded by .distignore, so any release build that skips the CI --no-dev step would ship test/static-analysis tooling to production and bloat the plugin artifact.
suggestion: Reset vendor/ to master and regenerate production-only: run 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader), commit only the production vendor (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler), and verify vendor/composer/installed.json no longer lists require-dev packages.

message: store_placeholder_data_for_upload() stores dominant-color/LQIP data only under the full-size original's rel_path, but the frontend lookup (get_placeholder_src_for_image(), class-image-optimisation.php:1986-2018) keys on the resolved path of the actually-rendered img URL. Content images typically render at sub-size URLs (e.g. -300x200.jpg) and the server-side path populates per-size entries because convert_image() runs for each queued size, so under WP 7.1 client-side processing every sub-size lookup misses and silently falls back to the SVG placeholder — the PR's headline outcome only holds for full-size renders.
suggestion: Pass $metadata into store_placeholder_data_for_upload() and, alongside the full-size entry, store the same dominant_color/lqip values under each sub-size rel_path in $metadata['sizes'] (sub-size files live in the same upload dir), mirroring the server-side per-size coverage so renders at any size hit the cache.

message: The return value of file_get_contents() is passed straight into imagecreatefromstring() without a check or try/catch. If the file disappears between the earlier file_exists()/filesize() checks and the read (a TOCTOU race on busy or network-mounted uploads dirs), file_get_contents() returns false and imagecreatefromstring(false) throws an uncaught TypeError in PHP 8 that the @ operator cannot suppress, propagating out of the wp_generate_attachment_metadata filter and failing the upload request.
suggestion: Capture the file contents, guard against false, and wrap the decode in a try/catch (\Throwable) returning silently on failure, matching the defensive pattern used elsewhere in the class.

message: The client-side branch runs before the exclude_imgs (excludeWebPImages) check that the server-side path applies (lines 922-928), so images the admin explicitly excluded from conversion still get a full file read + GD decode for placeholder extraction on every upload — an inconsistency between the two paths and unexpected per-upload work the user opted out of.
suggestion: Apply the same exclude_imgs URL-substring early-return at the top of the client-side branch before calling store_placeholder_data_for_upload(), mirroring lines 922-928, or move the exclusion check above the client-side branch so both paths share it.

message: The new method's docblock says @since 4.0.0, but the plugin is at version 1.8.0 and the sibling placeholder helpers are @since 3.0.0, which misleads maintainers about which release introduced the method.
suggestion: Change @since 4.0.0 to the next actual release version (e.g. @since 1.9.0).

message: No test coverage was added for the new client-side placeholder branch or the re-queue suppression, even though tests/php contains PHPUnit suites for sibling classes (class-image-optimisation-test.php, class-cache-test.php). The hook-registration gating, placeholderType guard, per-path cache writes, and add_img_into_queue() suppression are all easy to assert and would lock in the iteration-1 fixes against regression.
suggestion: Add PHPUnit cases that stub wp_is_client_side_media_processing_enabled() to true, upload a small PNG, assert dominant_color/lqip entries exist in wppo_img_info for the full-size (and, after the keying fix, sub-size) rel_paths, and assert add_img_into_queue() is not called from maybe_serve_next_gen_image() when client-side processing is enabled.

message: The re-queue suppression is gated on wp_is_client_side_media_processing_enabled(), a server-side secure-context flag, not a per-browser capability check. On HTTPS sites where the uploading browser lacks wasm-vips support and core silently falls back to server-side processing, new uploads are never queued — and when the site format is 'avif' (GD lacks AVIF, so core_handles_both_next_gen() is false), AVIF-supporting browsers are served the original format with nothing ever queued to convert it, silently stranding AVIF delivery.
suggestion: Document this tradeoff and/or additionally gate the suppression on the site actually having core handle both next-gen formats (core_handles_both_next_gen()), so the AVIF-only fallback still queues conversions when core cannot produce AVIF.

message: wp_is_client_side_media_processing_enabled() is invoked on every maybe_serve_next_gen_image() call — a per-image frontend hot path — even though $this->format is typically 'none' under WP 7.1 where neither format branch executes and the result is never used, adding a function_exists guard plus a core option read for every rendered image.
suggestion: Compute $client_side_processing lazily only inside the 'avif'/'webp'/'both' format branches where it is consumed, or cache it in a class-level static keyed by blog ID to avoid repeated core-option reads in the hot path.

message: The reachability fix covers only the WP 7.1 client-side branch. On WP 6.7-7.0, core_handles_next_gen() is already true (wp_image_quality exists) so get_format() maps the default webp/both to 'none' and $should_hook_conversion is false, while wp_is_client_side_media_processing_enabled() does not exist yet — so the wp_generate_attachment_metadata filter is still never registered and dominant-color/LQIP extraction remains silently unreachable on common modern configs.
suggestion: Extend the hook condition to also register the filter whenever core handles next-gen formats natively, so placeholder extraction is reachable on 6.7+ regardless of the client-side processing gate.
